source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Front Suspension, p.3-17

procedures.title: Lower control arm cross shaft and/or bushings: remove and install
steps: Move the capscrew to the other end of the shaft, turn the arm over on the support (bushing flange again clear) and press out the second bushing; discard it.
Installation: with the cross shaft in the arm and J-7052-1 in place, set the arm on J-5888-3 and start a bushing by hand into the arm over the shaft end.
Put installer J-7052-5 over the bushing; make sure the three-piece spacer does not overlap the bushing holes in the arm.
Press until the bushing flange meets the arm (see figure 29 in the manual).
Turn the arm over and press in the other bushing the same way; the shaft should then turn by hand.
Fit the collar, lock washer and capscrew at each end; torque to specification only after the spring is installed.
notes: The end of the cross shaft with two bolt holes goes toward the front of the arm.

procedures.title: Upper control arm spherical joint: inspect and replace
steps: Inspection: after replacement steps 1-4 below, put a nut on the stud and read the torque needed to turn the stud in the joint.
Replace the joint if the reading is far above or below specification; if the upper joint is worn, replace both upper and lower joints.
Replacement: support the car at the outer end of the lower control arm.
Remove the cotter pin and nut from the upper ball stud.
Free the stud from the knuckle.
Drill the joint holes in the arm out to 21/64" for the 5/16" bolts in the kit.
Fit the new joint with the special bolts and nuts supplied.
Reconnect the ball stud to the knuckle.

specs.what: upper joint ball stud turning torque, new joint

notes: The upper control arm does not have to be removed for this inspection.
Lube fittings: same as for the lower joint; new joints come without a fitting, so install a self-threading fitting in the untapped hole.
